lead: A class model names the things the problem talks about — patient, doctor, slot — and the links and rules between them. A behavioural model then shows how one thing changes state, or how several things exchange messages in one scenario. These models exist because prose hides gaps: a sentence like “patient books slot” does not say what a slot is, how many appointments a patient can hold, or what happens when a doctor cancels. Analysts draw them during requirements analysis, before design and code, to expose missing rules.
prereq: You need: scenarios from Chapter 2.6 and light UML notation from Unit 3.

blocks.text: A class is a template for things that share data and behaviour. An object is one instance. In the hospital problem, Patient is a class; the patient with token A-17 is an object. An attribute is a named fact kept for each object, such as patientId or slotTime. An operation is a service the class offers, such as bookSlot or cancel.

Look for three kinds of analysis class. An entity class is a thing the business must remember. A boundary class is the interface between an actor and the system, such as BookingScreen. A control class coordinates one use case, such as AppointmentCoordinator. Do not turn every screen field into a class: a field is usually an attribute of an entity, and a button is usually an operation or part of a boundary.
Some syllabi call this requirements modelling or analysis modelling. The model is conceptual; it is not yet a database schema.

An association is a link between classes that the business keeps. Each end has multiplicity: how many objects may take part. 1 means exactly one; 0..1 means zero or one; 0..* means zero or more; 1..* means at least one. The star is read “many”.

In the appointment model, Patient 1—0..* Appointment: one patient may have zero or more appointments. Doctor 1—0..* Slot: one doctor may own zero or more slots. Slot 1—0..1 Appointment: a slot may be free or may hold one appointment.

Generalization is an is-a link: Doctor is a Person. Aggregation is a whole-part link: a Ward has Patients, but a patient can exist without that ward. Do not use aggregation for every association. A data model uses entity, attribute, relationship and cardinality for the same facts; cardinality is another word for multiplicity. Draw multiplicities from business rules, not from what a screen shows today.

A state machine models one class over its life. A state is a condition the object can be in. An event is a happening that may cause a transition. A transition is an allowed move from one state to another. For Appointment, the states are requested, confirmed, cancelled and completed.

Transitions: requested → confirmed when the doctor accepts; requested → cancelled when patient or doctor cancels; confirmed → completed when the visit is done; confirmed → cancelled when the doctor cancels. Cancelled and completed are final for that appointment.

A sequence model shows one scenario as messages in time order: Patient → BookingScreen: book(slot); BookingScreen → Coordinator: check(slot); Coordinator → Slot: reserve(). An activity model shows a workflow with decisions: book slot → check slot free → create appointment or refuse. Use sequence for one scenario and activity for a process. Keep states as conditions, not actions.

examples.question: A hospital appointment system has 3 doctors and 30 slots per doctor per day. A patient books a slot; a doctor can cancel. An appointment moves through requested, confirmed, cancelled and completed. Identify the core classes, multiplicities and the state machine, and count the slots per day.
steps: Read the nouns the business must remember. The core entity classes are Patient, Doctor, Slot and Appointment. BookingScreen is a boundary class and AppointmentCoordinator is a control class; they are not the core entities.
Set multiplicities. One Patient links to 0..* Appointment. One Doctor links to 0..* Slot. One Slot links to 0..1 Appointment.
Count slots per day: 3 doctors × 30 slots per doctor = 90 Slot objects per day. If every slot is booked, the system has at most 90 appointments per day.
List states for Appointment: requested, confirmed, cancelled, completed. Count = 4.

List allowed transitions: requested→confirmed when the doctor accepts; requested→cancelled when patient or doctor cancels; confirmed→completed when the visit is done; confirmed→cancelled when the doctor cancels. Count = 4.
examples.answer: Classes are Patient, Doctor, Slot and Appointment; with 3 doctors and 30 slots per doctor the model has 90 slots per day; Appointment has 4 states and 4 transitions.
examples.check:
doctors = 3
slots_per_doctor = 30
slots_per_day = doctors * slots_per_doctor
states = 4
transitions = 4
print(doctors)
print(slots_per_doctor)
print(slots_per_day)
print(states)
print(transitions)

traps: Confusing a class with an object: Patient is a template; the patient with token A-17 is an object.
Making every screen field or button a class; prefer an attribute, an operation, or a boundary class.
Using actions as state names, such as “Cancel appointment” instead of cancelled; a state is a condition.
Reading 0..* as “one or more” or 1..* as “zero or more”; the star allows many, the leading number sets the minimum.
Using aggregation for every “has” link; aggregation is whole-part, not a general association.

quiz.a: A class is a template for things with shared data and behaviour. An object is one instance of that class at one time.

quiz.q: Why is “Cancel button” a poor class in an appointment model?
quiz.a: It is an interface element, not a business entity. It is better modelled as an operation on a boundary or control class.

quiz.q: A clinic has 4 doctors and 25 slots per doctor per day. How many Slot objects per day at most?
quiz.a: 4 doctors × 25 slots per doctor = 100 slots per day.

quiz.q: An appointment can be cancelled only from requested or confirmed. State the two cancellation transitions and their events.
quiz.a: requested→cancelled when the patient or doctor cancels; confirmed→cancelled when the doctor cancels.

quiz.q: What does 0..* mean on the Patient—Appointment association?
quiz.a: One patient may be linked to zero or more appointments; a patient with no appointment is allowed.

quiz.q: Why should “completed” not be used as an action state?
quiz.a: A state is a condition the object is in. Completion is an event that causes a transition into the completed condition.

quiz.q: For states requested, confirmed, cancelled, completed, list the allowed transitions and count them.

beyond: Not for the exam. Industry uses domain models as the first shared picture between business analysts and developers, and tools keep these models linked to requirements. Analysis patterns such as Information Holder, Party, Role and Accountability save time on recurring structures like patient and doctor. Search for “analysis patterns Fowler”, “domain model” and “model-based systems engineering” to go further.
